items.headline: High Surf Advisory issued September 7 at 1:29PM PDT until September 8 at 11:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
items.description:
* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 4 to 7 feet with sets up to 9
feet, highest at south and southwest-facing beaches. Strong and
dangerous rip and longshore currents. Minor coastal flooding
from a combination of high surf and high astronomical tides
during the evenings.

* WHERE...Beaches of Orange and San Diego Counties.

* WHEN...Through 11 PM PDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with isolated
road closures expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing
conditions and beach erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Predicted higher high tides:

Newport Beach: Today: 6.8 feet at 7:08 PM. Tuesday: 7.0 feet at
7:59 PM.
La Jolla: Today: 6.7 feet at 7:03 PM. Tuesday: High 6.9 feet at
7:54 PM PDT.
items.instruction:
It is extremely dangerous to fish or observe waves from exposed
coastal structures or rocks during high surf conditions. Very
large waves can suddenly sweep across previously dry areas.
Swimming or surfing in these waves may be dangerous for anyone
due to the powerful waves and strong rip currents.

Longshore currents commonly occur when waves approach the
shoreline at an angle. They can be particularly dangerous near a
jetty or pier.

items.headline: Heat Advisory issued September 7 at 11:09AM PDT until September 10 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
items.description:
* WHAT...High temperatures 85 to 95 degrees expected and overnight
lows in the mid 70s.

* WHERE...Orange County Coastal Areas and San Diego County Coastal
Areas.

* WHEN...From 10 AM Tuesday to 8 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures may cause heat illnesses.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Moderate to major HeatRisk. Elevated overnight
lows will limit relief from the heat.
items.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

items.headline: Marine Weather Statement issued September 7 at 6:51AM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
items.description:
Tropical moisture will continue to stream over the area and bring
a slight chance of thunderstorms to the coastal waters. Any
thunderstorm that forms will be capable of producing locally gale
force winds and rough seas, dangerous lightning, and brief heavy
rainfall with reduced visibility.
